properties.name: Crimea & Donbas (disputed)
properties.note: Crimea (annexed 2014) and parts of the Donbas — Donetsk and Luhansk — have been under Russian or Russian-backed de facto control since 2014, with four oblasts claimed/annexed by Russia in 2022; Ukraine and most of the international community recognize all of them as Ukrainian sovereign territory. Status disputed.

properties.name: Annexed oblasts (disputed)
properties.note: Russia declared the annexation of the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts in September 2022 alongside Donetsk and Luhansk; it does not fully control them and Ukraine and the international community recognize them as Ukrainian. Status disputed.

properties.name: Golan Heights (disputed)
properties.note: Israel has administered the Golan Heights since the 1967 war and applied its law in 1981; Syria claims the territory and most international bodies treat it as occupied Syrian land. Status disputed.

properties.name: West Bank & Gaza (disputed)
properties.bilingual: الضفة الغربية وغزة / West Bank & Gaza
properties.controller: Israel / Palestinian Authority / Hamas (mixed de facto)
properties.note: The West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza are claimed by the State of Palestine for a future state; Israel administers the West Bank and East Jerusalem and disputes their status, while Gaza was under Hamas de facto control after 2007. Most international bodies treat these areas as occupied/disputed. Status disputed.

properties.name: Kashmir (disputed)
properties.note: Disputed since 1947: India administers Jammu, the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh; Pakistan administers Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; China administers Aksai Chin. India and Pakistan each claim the whole of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. Status disputed.

properties.name: Northern Cyprus (disputed)
claimants: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (Kuzey Kıbrıs Türk Cumhuriyeti)
properties.controller: TRNC (de facto since 1974, recognized only by Turkey)
properties.note: After the 1974 conflict and the 1983 unilateral declaration of independence, the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus controls the northern third of the island but is recognized only by Turkey; the Republic of Cyprus and the UN regard the area as occupied territory of the Republic of Cyprus. Status disputed.

properties.name: Nagorno-Karabakh (disputed)
properties.controller: Republic of Artsakh (de facto 1991–2023, then Azerbaijan)
properties.note: Internationally recognized as part of Azerbaijan; de facto governed 1991–2023 by the Armenian-backed Republic of Artsakh (Nagorno-Karabakh Republic), which dissolved on 1 January 2024 after Azerbaijan reasserted control. Armenia and Azerbaijan dispute the territory's status. Status disputed.

properties.name: Southern Kuril Islands (disputed)
properties.bilingual: Курильские острова / 北方領土 / Northern Territories
properties.note: The southern Kuril Islands — Iturup/Etorofu, Kunashir/Kunashiri, Shikotan and the Habomai islets — have been administered by Russia (formerly the USSR) since Soviet forces occupied them in 1945, and are claimed by Japan as the 'Northern Territories' (Hoppō Ryōdo). The unresolved dispute has prevented a formal Russia-Japan WWII peace treaty. Status disputed.

properties.name: Xinjiang / East Turkestan (disputed)
properties.note: Administered by the People's Republic of China as the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region since 1949 (incorporating the short-lived 1944–1949 Second East Turkestan Republic). Uyghur and other Turkic movements call the territory 'East Turkestan' and contest Chinese sovereignty; the PRC and most states treat it as an integral part of China. Status disputed.

properties.name: Tibet (disputed)
properties.note: The People's Republic of China asserted control over Tibet around 1950, formalized by the 1951 Seventeen Point Agreement; the Tibetan government in Lhasa had administered it as a de facto independent state since 1913. Beijing regards Tibet as an integral part of China; the Tibetan government-in-exile contests the incorporation. Status disputed.

properties.name: Kosovo (disputed)
properties.controller: Republic of Kosovo (de facto, partial recognition)
properties.note: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 and is recognized by roughly half of UN member states; Serbia, backed by Russia, China and others, rejects the secession and considers the territory its Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija. Status disputed.

properties.name: Western Sahara (disputed)
claimants: Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic / Polisario (الجمهورية العربية الصحراوية الديمقراطية)
properties.note: A non-self-governing territory whose sovereignty is disputed: Morocco controls roughly the western 80% (its 'Southern Provinces') and claims the whole, while the Polisario Front's Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic controls the eastern 'Free Zone' and claims the territory, backed by UN/AU calls for a self-determination referendum. Status disputed.

properties.name: Taiwan (disputed)
claimants: People's Republic of China (中华人民共和国)
properties.controller: Republic of China (de facto, limited recognition)
properties.note: Taiwan is governed by the Republic of China (ROC), which exercises de facto control and considers itself a sovereign state; the People's Republic of China claims Taiwan as a province and rejects the ROC's separate sovereignty. International recognition is split under varying 'one China' formulations. Status disputed.
